data.note:
Reflection: Floxuridine (FUDR, 5-fluoro-deoxyuridine, PubChem CID 5790) identity confirmed (e20) – ChEMBL CHEMBL917: Thymidylate synthase inhibitor, annotated in BBBC021 as DNA replication. Mechanistically depletes dTTP via thymidylate synthase (TS) inhibition, causing S-phase stress.

My call of Aurora kinase inhibitors was wrong. Phenotype showed massive cell_area z=+23.5, nuc_area enlargement, frac_large_nucleus, transient frac_mitotic_like spike at 1uM (e2,e11) with diffuse tubulin (e13≈0). Microscopist suggested Aurora polyploidy (e4). However atlas for the critical 1uM well (e16) actually favored DNA replication (mean similarity 0.766 for mitoxantrone/methotrexate) over Aurora (0.692 for AZ-A), with top neighbours e6/e16: mitoxantrone 0.81/0.85 and methotrexate 0.73 – both DNA replication antimetabolites. I over-weighted the single-dose mitotic artefact (n=1, non-monotonic rho=0.0, e11) and morphology.

Literature supports DNA-replication phenotype mimicking Aurora: Floxuridine/FUDR triggers intra-S checkpoint and translesion synthesis tolerance via REV3 (PMID 38954736) and mismatch repair-mediated cell cycle checkpoint response to fluorodeoxyuridine (PMID 18543256) – consistent with S-phase arrest and enlarged nuclei. Drug-induced megaloblastic change from TS inhibition (PMID 6450011) explains hypertrophic cell/nuclear enlargement (cell_area, cell_nuc_area_ratio e2,e7,e8) without true mitotic arrest. TS synthesis regulation in FUDR-resistant fibroblasts (PMID 3155521) and deoxyribonucleoside modulation of cytotoxicity (PMID 3158302) further document TS-dependent replication stress.

Lesson: large spread cells + pale enlarged nuclei are not specific to failed cytokinesis; requires phospho-H3 Ser10 + ploidy flow to separate Aurora (p-H3 loss/polyploidy) from replication stress (intra-S checkpoint). PI-requested replicate 2 at 1µM could not be acquired (budget 0/4 spent) – would have tested reproducibility of the anomalous spike.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: floxuridine - PubChem CID 5790, ChEMBL CHEMBL917, Thymidylate synthase inhibitor (CHEMBL1952) - MoA class "DNA replication" in BBBC021 ontology. Agent called Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.58 -> 0.52) - incorrect. Verdict correct:false.

What the evidence got right vs misled:

1. Correct rejections were sound. tub_mean dose response rho=+0.00 p=1 (e13) with 4 wells correctly excluded microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers. e2/e3 massive cell_area z=+23.5 at 1uM, +13.6 at 100uM and cell_nuc_area_ratio elevations correctly excluded actin disruptors / cholesterol-lowering / epithelial classes (hypotheses 0.00, e3, e7, e8). Cell count modest negative rho=-0.40 p=0.6 (e12) and density lower vs DMSO (e4, e5) was consistent with cytotoxic S-phase arrest, not ruled out.

2. What misled: massive morphometric enlargement was over-interpreted as Aurora polyploidy. e2: cell_area +23.5, frac_large_nucleus +14.6, cell_major_axis +11.9 at 1uM (55 cells); e7: cell_area +14.1 at 0.1uM; e3/e8: cell_nuc_area_ratio +9.3/+7.6. Thymidylate synthase inhibition produces the same phenotype: drug-induced megaloblastic change with enlarged nuclei/cells due to unbalanced growth during thymineless S-phase arrest PMID 6450011, and 5-fluorodeoxyuridine specifically activates translesion synthesis and intra-S checkpoint PMID 38954736 and mismatch repair-mediated cell cycle checkpoint response PMID 18543256. The agent treated this as Aurora-specific failed cytokinesis.

3. Anthropogenic anchoring: describe_phenotype e4 "candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors" on 6 observations, even with only 2 fields, anchored the hypotheses (0.58 Aurora vs 0.22 DNA replication at step 14). describe_phenotype e5 at high dose returned "unknown" on 10 observations - should have down-weighted Aurora - but was not.

4. Atlas was misread as confirmatory. compare_to_reference_atlas e6 and e16 both: Aurora 5/10, DNA replication 3/10, DNA damage 2/10. Correct MoA was consistently present at 30% of neighbours - not distant. We cited "5/10" as favoring Aurora over DNA replication, without acknowledging that DNA replication + DNA damage = 5/10 equally, exactly what thymidylate synthase inhibition mimics morphologically.

5. Dose-response clues were missed due to acquisition design. e10 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.80 p=0.2 and e9 nuc_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2 across 4 wells indicate decreasing (not increasing) DNA content/nuclear area with dose - opposite of expected Aurora polyploidy dose-dependent increase. p=0.2 reflects n=4 wells power, not evidence of no effect, but direction should have triggered S-phase stalling hypothesis. e11 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.00 p=1 shows no mitotic dose trend, contradicting the single-well "mitotic spike" at 1uM used in rationale for e14/e15. e16/e17 we correctly noted contradiction (e11, e10) but probability only moved 0.58->0.52.

6. Acquisition choice caused the failure to correct: list_available_experiments offered 8 doses, budget 4/4 wells. We consumed all 4 on a sparse dose-tiling (0.1, 1, 10, 100uM, rep 1 only, e2,e3,e7,e8). No replicate was retained. Review requested acquire dose index 3 replicate 2 (1uM) to repeat the anomalous mitotic spike and re-compare atlas separation Aurora vs DNA-replication. Budget already spent, so steps 16-18 could only re-run compare_to_reference_atlas on existing well w_1777b23edf, no new profile. Intentional experiment was phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 + ploidy flow to test polyploidy vs S-phase arrest, which was never executable under this image-only run; that orthogonal readout is what distinguishes fluorodeoxyuridine S-checkpoint from Aurora failed cytokinesis.

Lesson: In BBBC021 floxuridine/fluoropyrimidine space, extreme cell/nuclear enlargement plus 3/10 DNA replication atlas votes should be treated as thymidylate synthase / DNA replication stress until proven otherwise, not as Aurora. Future runs should reserve 1 well for replication of intermediate-dose outlier before submitting, and weigh negative nuc_dna_integrated dose trend as counter-evidence to polyploidy, even when p>0.05 due to n=4.
what_was_right: Excluded microtubule/actin/cholesterol classes via tub_mean flat (e13) and cell shape metrics (e2,e3)
Atlas did contain truth at 3/10 DNA replication (e6,e16) - not an atlas failure
Dose-response direction for DNA content decreasing (e10 rho=-0.80) was inconsistent with Aurora
what_was_wrong: Over-weighted e4 microscopist Aurora call and e2 extreme cell_area z=+23.5 as Aurora-specific; same seen in thymineless megaloblastic change PMID 6450011
Ignored e11 rho=0.00 showing mitotic fraction not dose-dependent, and e5 unknown call
Spent all 4 wells without replicate, blocking requested verification of 1uM spike

5-fluorodeoxyuridine activates intra-S checkpoint/translesion synthesis consistent with S-phase arrest not mitotic failure
fluorodeoxyuridine triggers mismatch repair-mediated cell cycle checkpoint response

Unblinded truth: floxuridine - PubChem CID 5790, ChEMBL CHEMBL917, Thymidylate synthase inhibitor (CHEMBL1952) - MoA class "DNA replication" in BBBC021 ontology. Agent called Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.58 -> 0.52) - incorrect. Verdict correct:false.

What the evidence got right vs misled:

1. Correct rejections were sound. tub_mean dose response rho=+0.00 p=1 (e13) with 4 wells correctly excluded microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers. e2/e3 massive cell_area z=+23.5 at 1uM, +13.6 at 100uM and cell_nuc_area_ratio elevations correctly excluded actin disruptors / cholesterol-lowering / epithelial classes (hypotheses 0.00, e3, e7, e8). Cell count modest negative rho=-0.40 p=0.6 (e12) and density lower vs DMSO (e4, e5) was consistent with cytotoxic S-phase arrest, not ruled out.

2. What misled: massive morphometric enlargement was over-interpreted as Aurora polyploidy. e2: cell_area +23.5, frac_large_nucleus +14.6, cell_major_axis +11.9 at 1uM (55 cells); e7: cell_area +14.1 at 0.1uM; e3/e8: cell_nuc_area_ratio +9.3/+7.6. Thymidylate synthase inhibition produces the same phenotype: drug-induced megaloblastic change with enlarged nuclei/cells due to unbalanced growth during thymineless S-phase arrest PMID 6450011, and 5-fluorodeoxyuridine specifically activates translesion synthesis and intra-S checkpoint PMID 38954736 and mismatch repair-mediated cell cycle checkpoint response PMID 18543256. The agent treated this as Aurora-specific failed cytokinesis.

3. Anthropogenic anchoring: describe_phenotype e4 "candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors" on 6 observations, even with only 2 fields, anchored the hypotheses (0.58 Aurora vs 0.22 DNA replication at step 14). describe_phenotype e5 at high dose returned "unknown" on 10 observations - should have down-weighted Aurora - but was not.

4. Atlas was misread as confirmatory. compare_to_reference_atlas e6 and e16 both: Aurora 5/10, DNA replication 3/10, DNA damage 2/10. Correct MoA was consistently present at 30% of neighbours - not distant. We cited "5/10" as favoring Aurora over DNA replication, without acknowledging that DNA replication + DNA damage = 5/10 equally, exactly what thymidylate synthase inhibition mimics morphologically.

5. Dose-response clues were missed due to acquisition design. e10 nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.80 p=0.2 and e9 nuc_area rho=-0.80 p=0.2 across 4 wells indicate decreasing (not increasing) DNA content/nuclear area with dose - opposite of expected Aurora polyploidy dose-dependent increase. p=0.2 reflects n=4 wells power, not evidence of no effect, but direction should have triggered S-phase stalling hypothesis. e11 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.00 p=1 shows no mitotic dose trend, contradicting the single-well "mitotic spike" at 1uM used in rationale for e14/e15. e16/e17 we correctly noted contradiction (e11, e10) but probability only moved 0.58->0.52.

6. Acquisition choice caused the failure to correct: list_available_experiments offered 8 doses, budget 4/4 wells. We consumed all 4 on a sparse dose-tiling (0.1, 1, 10, 100uM, rep 1 only, e2,e3,e7,e8). No replicate was retained. Review requested acquire dose index 3 replicate 2 (1uM) to repeat the anomalous mitotic spike and re-compare atlas separation Aurora vs DNA-replication. Budget already spent, so steps 16-18 could only re-run compare_to_reference_atlas on existing well w_1777b23edf, no new profile. Intentional experiment was phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 + ploidy flow to test polyploidy vs S-phase arrest, which was never executable under this image-only run; that orthogonal readout is what distinguishes fluorodeoxyuridine S-checkpoint from Aurora failed cytokinesis.

Lesson: In BBBC021 floxuridine/fluoropyrimidine space, extreme cell/nuclear enlargement plus 3/10 DNA replication atlas votes should be treated as thymidylate synthase / DNA replication stress until proven otherwise, not as Aurora. Future runs should reserve 1 well for replication of intermediate-dose outlier before submitting, and weigh negative nuc_dna_integrated dose trend as counter-evidence to polyploidy, even when p>0.05 due to n=4.

What was right:
- Excluded microtubule/actin/cholesterol classes via tub_mean flat (e13) and cell shape metrics (e2,e3)
- Atlas did contain truth at 3/10 DNA replication (e6,e16) - not an atlas failure
- Dose-response direction for DNA content decreasing (e10 rho=-0.80) was inconsistent with Aurora

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted e4 microscopist Aurora call and e2 extreme cell_area z=+23.5 as Aurora-specific; same seen in thymineless megaloblastic change PMID 6450011
- Ignored e11 rho=0.00 showing mitotic fraction not dose-dependent, and e5 unknown call
- Spent all 4 wells without replicate, blocking requested verification of 1uM spike

Proposed next experiment: Acquire dose index 3 replicate 2 (1uM floxuridine) plus randomized DMSO control; acquire EdU pulse + phospho-H3 Ser10 + Hoechst DNA content on same plate; compare replicated profile to atlas and test S-phase accumulation vs G2/M polyploidy to separate DNA replication (thymidylate synthase) from Aurora inhibition
